chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said: Abu Bilal al-Makki narrated to me saying:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) circumambulate the House (Kaaba), then pray two cycles between the door and the Black Stone. So I said to him: I have not seen any of you pray in this place. He replied: This is the place where Adam's repentance was accepted.

key_terms.الْحَجَرُ الْأَسْوَدُ: The Black Stone — sacred stone embedded in the corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.تِيبَ: Passive form of 'to repent' (taba) — the repentance was accepted/granted
key_terms.طَافَ: Performed tawaf — ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: Where in the Kaaba was Adam's repentance accepted according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Abu Bilal al-Makki, a Meccan witness, observed Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) perform two cycles of prayer in a specific spot between the Kaaba's door and the Black Stone — a location unusual in practice. When questioned, the Imam revealed the theological significance of that exact spot: it was the very place where Prophet Adam's (AS) repentance was accepted by God. This hadith connects Hajj rituals to the earliest sacred history and illuminates the spiritual geography of the Masjid al-Haram.
